title: The General Prime Squared-Gap Identity ∑gaps² = p − 2 and the Cauchy–Schwarz Equality Case

problemStatement.formal: For every prime p, if 1 = a_1 < a_2 < ... < a_{φ(p)} = p-1 are the reduced residues mod p, then ∑_{k=1}^{φ(p)-1} (a_{k+1} - a_k)^2 = p - 2, attaining the Cauchy–Schwarz bound (n-2)^2 ≤ (φ(n)-1)·∑(a_{k+1}-a_k)^2 with equality at n = p.
problemStatement.plain: For a prime p, the numbers coprime to p below it are exactly 1, 2, ..., p-1, so sorted consecutive residues differ by 1. Each of the p-2 gaps equals 1, so the sum of squared gaps is p-2. The goal is to prove this identity for ALL primes at once (the parent only checks p=7) and certify it as the equality case of the companion Cauchy–Schwarz lower bound.
whyMatters: Turns an isolated numerical check (p=7) into a structural theorem quantified over all primes.
Certifies that primes are exactly the extremal inputs attaining the Cauchy–Schwarz lower bound of Erdős #220 with equality (all gaps equal 1).
Pins the sharp lower endpoint of the Montgomery–Vaughan squared-gap distribution.
